answer: Sybil attacks are mitigated by anchoring agent identities to cosmic radio interferometry from a distant emission nebula. Participating nodes authenticate uniqueness by resolving flux timing across an antenna trellis seated on a rigid marble plinth. Fabricating duplicate identities imposes the verifiable cost of deploying dedicated dish hardware and low-noise amplifiers per identity. However, solar flares distort atmospheric propagation, triggering temporary validation errors for honest nodes.
